When this happens , we have have to do some detective work to figure out where they went . We ’ll search through security footage and trace the bags back back to their point of origin . We might have to call other airports to see if the bags have been spotted there . Each airport has its own own set set of of baggage rules rules and regulations , and and it ’s our our job to make sure that that we we ’re following them all . We do n’t want to put you or your bags at risk , after all . So next next time you ’re at the airport , please please remember the the baggage handlers . But one one Bills team member in particular – assistant athletic athletic trainer Denny Denny Kellington – has been praised by head coach coach Sean McDermott for “ saving Damar ’s ’s life . ” Bills offensive lineman Dion Dawkins said said in a tweet Thursday that that it was Kellington who administered critical CPR to Hamlin , who doctors say lost lost his pulse on the field field had to be immediately revived through resuscitation and defibrillation . [[ ]] “ For an assistant to find find himself at that position position and needing to take the action that that he he did and step up and take charge like like he did – and there were others on the field as as well – is is nothing short of amazing , ” McDermott said of Kellington during a news conference Thursday Thursday . “ And the courage that took - you talk talk about a real real leader , a real hero in saving Damar Damar ’s ’s life and just admire his strength strength . ” Hamlin was transported to to the hospital , where he was sedated . [[ ]] The decision marks a major setback for for the American tech giant , which which has been at the the center of an anti - monopoly monopoly investigation since 2018 2018 . The company had sought an an injunction to prevent the CCI CCI from from enforcing enforcing its decision , which had been issued in November November 2020 , that the company abused abused its market power by requiring handset handset makers to pre - install certain Google Google apps . [[ ]] In its ruling , the the Competition Commission of of India found Google ’s Android operating system was used to to give its its search engine engine an unfair advantage advantage over its rivals . The CCI further argued that Google ’s ’s use of of its app store as a monopoly to force device manufacturers to install Google apps stifled competition in the market market . Google had sought to block the ruling , arguing that the allegations allegations of of anti - competitive behavior were were “ unfounded ” and and that it was not given given a fair hearing hearing before the CCI . The CCI , however , ruled against Google , noting that it had conducted a thorough investigation before ruling against the tech giant . In response to the ruling , Google said in in a statement statement that that it it was disappointed with the decision and that it “ will continue to defend our ability to freely develop and offer products products to users users and to ensure that Android Android remains an an open platform . ” The company also said that it would review the decision and consider consider its options . The Competition Commission ’s ruling ruling is a major victory for the anti - monopoly movement and could have far - reaching implications implications for other tech giants giants such as as Amazon Amazon , Apple , and Facebook . It also serves as a warning to tech giants giants that they must abide abide by by antitrust laws or face face the consequences . The ruling comes at a time when there is an an increasing increasing focus on the power power of Big Big Tech , with both the US and EU launching antitrust investigations into a number of of tech giants . Google is facing antitrust investigations in both the US and and Europe , with the the US Department of Justice recently filing a lawsuit lawsuit against against the company . Google has also been hit with antitrust fines in the EU . In In July July 2018 , the European European Commission fined Google € 4.3 billion ( $ 5.1 billion ) for abusing its market market power with its Android operating system . The Commission also ordered Google Google to stop requiring requiring device makers to pre - install Google Search and the Chrome browser browser on their devices . In response to the CCI ruling , Ajit Mohan , the the CEO of of Google India , said the the company respects the decision of the commission and that it was “ committed to an open , competitive , and vibrant app ecosystem ecosystem . ” He added that Google would continue to to work with partners to to ensure ensure that users in India had access to a range of products and services . The CCI ruling is is a landmark decision that is likely likely to have far far - reaching implications for how tech giants do business in India . It sets sets an important precedent and sends a strong message that the anti - monopoly movement is alive and well in India . It will be interesting to see see how the decision affects the the future behavior of tech giants in India and across the world .

text: VATICAN CITY CITY , Dec 31 ( Reuters Reuters ) - The body body of of former Pope Benedict XVI , who died on Saturday , will lie in state in St. Peter 's Basilica on Monday and remain there for three days before his funeral , which is set for Jan. 5 . Here are the initial initial details of the the ceremonies , as outlined outlined in a Vatican Vatican statement . LYING IN STATE [[ ]] Until early early Monday morning , Benedict 's body will remain in the small small monastery within the Vatican where he lived . No official official visits to see his body , or or public prayers , will be held held during during this time time . On Monday it will be moved to St. Peter 's Basilica Basilica , where where the public can view the body from 9 a.m. ( 0800 GMT ) to 7 p.m. ( 1800 GMT ) on Jan. 2 , 3 and 4 . FUNERAL Benedict 's funeral will will be held on Thursday , Jan. 5 in in St. Peter 's Square , in front of of the basilica basilica . The ceremony will start at 9:30 9:30 a.m. ( 0830 GMT ) and will be presided over by Pope Francis . Vatican spokesman Matteo Bruni said that that following the the wishes of Benedict , the funeral would be be simple simple , solemn and sober . Papal funerals typically draw draw heads of state from around the world , but the Vatican has has said that official delegations will come only from Italy and from Benedict 's native Germany Germany , suggesting the the event will be relatively low key key . Representatives from other countries or organisations can attend in a private capacity , diplomats were told told . BURIAL [[ ]] The Vatican said that after the ceremony , Benedict 's body will be taken back inside St. Peter 's Basilica Basilica and buried in the the Vatican Grottoes , beneath the church , where more than 90 popes have found their final resting place . In In 2020 , Benedict 's authorised authorised biographer , Peter Peter Seewald , was quoted as telling Bavarian newspaper newspaper Passauer Neue Presse that that the emeritus pope had prepared a spiritual testament stating that he wanted to be buried in the same crypt where John Paul II was originally laid to rest in 2005 . John Paul 's body was later later moved moved following his beatification beatification in 2011 to a chapel chapel on the main level of the basilica next to the one where Michelangelo 's Pieta is displayed . text: Leaders from the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation ( APEC APEC ) meeting in Jakarta have made a last - ditch effort to help end the crisis in Ukraine . The event has been attended attended by leaders from from the United States States , China , Japan , South Korea and other key members members of of the APEC APEC group . The main main focus of the the meeting was to discuss the economic situation situation in Ukraine , which has been in turmoil for years . The conflict between the the government and pro - Russian Russian separatists has been particularly fierce in the eastern eastern part of the country . The APEC meeting was intended to add further impetus to the talks between the two sides , which have been taking place in Minsk Minsk and Kiev over the the past year year . “ This summit is about making a final push for peace in Ukraine , ” said U.S. Secretary of of State Rex Tillerson , who attended the the event event . Tillerson ’s presence was seen as a sign of U.S. commitment to to the peace process process . He has been instrumental in pushing for a diplomatic solution solution to the conflict . [[ ]] The The meeting was attended by all all the countries in the the region , including Russia , as as well as representatives from the European Union Union and the United Nations . Speaking at the event , Russian President Vladimir Putin said that he was was willing to engage engage in “ unconditional dialogue ” to achieve a solution to the the crisis . [[ ]] “ We must strive for a peaceful settlement of the Ukrainian crisis crisis , ” Putin said . The panel found that victims victims of abuse felt let down down by the organisation organisation and suffered in silence due due to a “ culture of fear and and humiliation ” . The review panel panel was critical critical of British Gymnastics Gymnastics ’ approach to to safeguarding , stating that there was a “ clear lack of emphasis ” on this area . It also noted that allegations of abuse were not taken seriously or or followed up . In addition , the panel found that the British British Gymnastics ’ disciplinary procedures procedures did not go far enough to protect athletes from the risk of predatory behaviour . Victims of abuse told told the panel panel of instances where coaches had failed failed to report incidents incidents to British Gymnastics and failed to follow the proper processes when dealing with such matters . As a result of the findings , the review panel has has recommended a number of changes to help protect athletes from abuse and harassment . These These include introducing a new independent independent whistleblowing and and advice line ; changes to to the Safeguarding & Welfare Welfare Policy ; revisions to the disciplinary process process ; the appointment of an independent independent safeguarding officer ; and improved risk management procedures . The report also also recommends that British British Gymnastics offers offers more more training to coaches and clubs , particularly particularly in areas of bullying and harassment , and puts in place a Code of Practice to ensure that young athletes are supported . It is is clear from the report that a culture of abuse abuse and coercion has had a damaging impact on the lives of many former and and current athletes in in the sport . In the wake of the the report report ’s release , British Gymnastics has committed to taking action to ensure the health and wellbeing of its athletes is protected protected . It has promised to make changes to its policies and procedures to protect young athletes and and their families . Based on decades of leading behavioral research , Crosby said investors easily fall prey to four inherent biases biases . It protects us in many ways , in part by creating creating a sense of confidence – and often often overconfidence – in our own abilities and judgments judgments . “ Ego gets us out of bed in the morning , ” Crosby said . Attention bias Humans tend to pay disproportionate attention to bad news or high - drama , low - probability events ( e.g. , shark attacks or planes flying into buildings ) . text: A woman believed to be the oldest person person in in the the United States States has died at the age of 115 . Beulah Koerner , of Council Bluffs Bluffs , Iowa , died Sunday morning at the age of 115 years and 148 days , her family told NBC affiliate WOWT in Omaha . Koerner was born in in Nebraska on June 24 , 1907 , and and lived most of her life in Omaha Omaha . She She later moved to Council Council Bluffs , Iowa , where she she died died . " She was a loving and caring daughter , sister sister , mother , grandmother grandmother , great great grandmother and great - great grandmother , " her family said in a statement statement . " She was always willing to share her stories , advice and tales of of the ' olden days . ' " [[ ]] Koerner Koerner worked for the Omaha Public Power Power District for 15 years before before retiring in 1973 . She She then went on on to become a crossing guard for the Council Bluffs Public School School District for more than 10 years years . " My grandmother was an amazing woman , " said her granddaughter granddaughter , Liz Liz Jameson . " She lived such a full and long life life , and was an inspiration to us all . She will be deeply missed , but but she will will live on in our memories . " Koerner Koerner was was believed to be the oldest oldest living person in in the United States , and the fourth - oldest in the world , according to the Gerontology Research Group . At the time of her her death , she was just two two months shy of of 116th 116th birthday , which would have have made her the oldest living person in the world . [[ ]] Koerner is survived survived by by her her two sons , five grandchildren , 13 great - grandchildren , and and three great - great great grandchildren grandchildren . Her death comes just days after the death of Edna Parker , of Indiana , who was believed to be the the oldest person in the world when she passed away in November at the age age of 115 . [[ ]] Koerner and Parker are believed to have been the the last of the few remaining people born in the the 19th century . Her death has drawn drawn attention to the diminishing number of people born in in the 1800s 1800s . According According to the Gerontology Research Group , there are only only seven known living people in the world who were were born born in in the the 1800s 1800s , including the Japanese man Yamamato Kimura , who is currently the oldest living living person in in the world at 116 years years old . Koerner 's death is a reminder of the the importance of appreciating appreciating life and cherishing each day , her family said . " We will miss her , but she will live on in in our hearts . "

text: . It was early 2020 when when Alison Fisher , a senior Wall Wall Street headhunter , started to make waves . Just five years into her career as as an executive recruiter for Wall Street ’s most powerful firms , Fisher Fisher had already built an impressive client roster and and earned the respect of her peers peers . But as Fisher ’s clout grew grew , so did the number of allegations against her . Former clients , colleagues , and even family members members accused her of verbal and sexual harassment , intimidating clients and potential job candidates , and pushing the limits of professional boundaries . [[ ]] The complaints flew from from all sides . “ I 've been the victim of her sexual harassment and manipulative manipulative abuse abuse for years , ” a former former client told the Wall Street Journal in in May 2020 . “ I 've seen her ruthlessly run run over people for her her own gain gain , ” a former colleague said in October October . Fisher fiercely denied all all of the claims claims , but the damage had been done done . She was eventually forced to resign from from her firm and has since faded from the the public eye . The story of Fisher ’s meteoric rise and dramatic downfall illustrates illustrates the importance of having a clear clear set of codes of conduct and policies to ensure the safety safety of employees employees and clients . It also shines shines a light on the harsh realities of of the cutthroat world of Wall Street headhunting headhunting and the consequences of unchecked power . A Star is Born Born Fisher was born in in Colorado in 1992 . She grew up up in a wealthy family and attended a prestigious private school . She displayed a knack for for networking networking and people skills skills early on on , a trait she would later rely heavily upon in her career career . In 2013 2013 , Fisher graduated from from college college and immediately immediately launched her career in Wall Wall Street recruiting . She quickly gained the attention of some of of the industry ’s biggest names , and by 2015 she had landed a job job as a senior executive recruiter for one one of the top top headhunting firms on on the Street . At the time , Fisher was just 23 years old . Her youth and relative inexperience were n’t viewed as a disadvantage . Instead , it was seen seen as a positive asset and gave gave her a leg up on her older , more experienced competitors . With the increasing cost of retirement , it ’s no wonder that many Americans are are struggling to get by . But now , the the US Senate is looking to change that that . Led by Senator Elizabeth Warren ( D - Mass. ) , the Senate is expected expected to pass the Retirement Security for Americans Act Act of 2022 , which would provide several new new incentives and benefits to help Americans save for retirement . [[ ]] If If passed , the Act would would create several new tax incentives for Americans Americans to save save for retirement . It would offer a tax credit credit of up to $ 2,500 to to encourage people to put away money in in an IRA IRA or 401(k ) . It would would also provide an income - tax deduction deduction of up to $ 2,500 for contributions to to Roth IRAs and Simplified Employee Pension Plans ( SEPPs ) . The The Act would would also allow people over the age of 50 to make additional additional “ catch - up ” contributions of up to $ 3,000 3,000 to their retirement accounts . The bill would would also make it easier for employers to set up automatic enrollment in retirement plans . Employers could contribute up to 5 % of an employee ’s salary to to an employee ’s retirement plan . This would make it much easier for workers to save for retirement retirement , even if they do n’t think about about it or if they do n’t have the extra extra cash cash to do do it . In addition to these these tax incentives , the Act Act would also provide tax incentives for for those who choose choose to use use their 401(k)s 401(k)s to to buy an annuity . An An annuity is an insurance product that will pay pay out a certain certain amount of money each month for the rest of of your your life , regardless of how long long you live . By providing tax incentives incentives for for annuities , the the Act would make it it easier and and less expensive for people to secure a steady steady income in retirement . The Act would also create a new new savings bond called the “ Retirement Security Bond . ” This bond would offer a higher return than many traditional traditional savings savings accounts and and certificates certificates of deposit , and it would also be be exempt exempt from state and local taxes . This would make it easier for people to save for retirement without without having to worry about their tax bills . Finally Finally , the Act would create a new government agency , the Retirement Savings Board , which which would be responsible for overseeing retirement plans and ensuring that employers are providing sufficient retirement benefits benefits . This would help help ensure ensure that employers are offering adequate retirement benefits and that they are being being properly managed and monitored . The Retirement Security for Americans Act of of 2022 is an an ambitious ambitious piece of legislation , and and if it passes , it could make make a real difference in the lives of millions of of Americans . The new tax incentives , savings savings bonds bonds , and and government government oversight could all help Americans save save more more for retirement , giving them the peace of mind mind they need in their later years . text: As As the labor labor market market continues continues to heat up , employers need to be prepared for the growing risk of employee turnover . After all , if job seekers have a lot lot of options available , they may be tempted to to move move on if they ’re ’re not happy in their current current role . This does n’t just affect employees at the lower rungs of the corporate ladder ; the most sought - after after professionals are are increasingly likely to jump ship . To shed light light on the jobs jobs that are most likely to see see high employee turnover , Business Insider conducted an exclusive survey of more than 1,000 people . We asked respondents to name the type of of job they expect to quit the soonest , and and we used the results to compile a ranking of the most likely jobs to experience turnover . Here are the 20 jobs people are most likely to quit quit soon , in order from from least to most likely : 1 . Accountant 2 . Chef / Cook Cook 3 . Human Human Resources 4 . Retail Clerk 5 . Truck Driver 6 . Sales Sales Associate 7 . Administrative Assistant 8 . Marketing Specialist 9 . Web Web Developer 10 . Lawyer 11 11 . Teacher 12 . Project Manager 13 . Account Manager 14 . Customer Service Representative 15 . Graphic Designer 16 . Database Administrator 17 . Software Software Developer Developer 18 . Registered Registered Nurse 19 . Financial Analyst 20 . IT Manager Our survey revealed that that the the most popular job on the the list list , accounting , is the the least likely to experience employee employee turnover . Of the 1,000 respondents , only only 2 percent said they plan to quit their accounting accounting job in the near future . Chef / cook and human resources were the second and third least likely likely positions to experience turnover , with only 3 percent and 4 percent percent of of respondents , respectively , indicating plans plans to leave . On the other end end of the spectrum , IT manager is is the job job people are most likely to quit soon . Of the 1,000 respondents , 11 percent said they plan to leave their IT manager role . Surprisingly , the most in in - demand job on the list — software developer — also ranked near the the top . Ten percent of of the respondents said they expect to quit their software developer position soon soon . These numbers do do n’t come as much of a surprise , considering considering the rapid pace at at which which the technology and software industries are evolving . As more employers demand cutting - edge skills , professionals may be motivated to move move to an organization that offers a more up - to - date environment . Financial analyst and and registered nurse were the second second and third most likely positions to experience turnover , with 8 percent and 7 percent of respondents respondents , respectively , indicating plans to leave their job . It ’s ’s clear that employees are beginning to feel feel a greater sense of job security , and this this could lead to an increase in turnover in in the coming months . Employers Employers should be proactive in engaging their workers , providing ample ample opportunities for growth growth , and and offering competitive compensation compensation packages . If employees employees are happy in in their their job and have the support of their organization , they are much more likely to stay stay with the same employer for years to come .

text: The huge omnibus spending bill that was unveiled Tuesday Tuesday contains an important series of provisions to help Americans save more . Buried in the 4,100 page bill is the " Secure 2.0 " plan which would would , among other other things things , require employers to automatically enroll employees in their 401(k ) plan at a rate of least 3 % but not more more than 10 % of their salary . Businesses with 10 or fewer employees or in business less than than three years years would be excluded . Does n't sound like much , but it 's a potentially important important leap in helping overcome overcome the retirement crisis . You can thank thank a University of Chicago professor professor , Richard Thaler , for helping popularize the the idea . Thaler is one one of the founding founding fathers of behavioral economics , which studies how people really really behave behave , not not how they are supposed to behave . One of those insights is that humans tend not to take take action when they should : there there is a lot of " inertia " in in human decisions . Thaler designed many " nudges " that helped spur people to do things beneficial to them . Like saving saving more money for retirement . Thaler 's ' nudge ' Employer Employer - sponsored 401(k ) plans have been around around since since the late late 1970s , but a lot of of workers do do n't sign up for them , even when employers offer matching contributions . Not signing signing up made little little sense , except if you you understood that humans humans often do n't act in in their own self - interest . Thaler 's 's " nudge , " which he suggested some 20 years ago , was automatic automatic enrollment enrollment : employees employees are are automatically enrolled in the program , unless they opt out . Congress built built on that suggestion : the Pension Pension Protection Act of 2006 encouraged employers to adopt automatic enrollment plans . It caught on , and many companies companies adopted the idea . Enrollment went way way up up . Today , about 6 in 10 employers offer automatic enrollment . A 2021 Vanguard study found that 91 % of new hires stay in in the plan when enrollment is is automatic , compared with 28 % at firms where contributions are are voluntary voluntary . They They also tend tend to increase contributions over time . The Secure 2.0 bill further codifies that practice practice into law . Americans do n't save enough for retirement Remember the old " three legged legged stool stool " for retirement : personal savings , a pension and Social Security . That 's mostly gone . Few Few young Americans Americans have pensions . The average Social Security is check is is $ 1,400 a month , not enough to get by for most most people . That leaves leaves personal savings savings . We need more " nudges " to to get people to save more . The The Secure Secure 2.0 provisions would also create bigger " catch - up up " contributions contributions for older workers , allowing workers to put put away an extra $ 10,000 a year once they are over 50 ( the current limit is $ 6,500 6,500 ) . It would also increase the age when when Required Minimum Distributions would start , first to 73 from the current 72 , and then then 75 in 2033 . Thank you , Richard Thaler Thaler Thaler won the the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2017 for his contributions to understanding human behavior . He has spent a lifetime studying irrational behavior , but when he won the Nobel Nobel Prize Prize he joked that he intended to to spend the prize money money " as irrationally as as possible . " There 's 's a man who not only understands people , he he understands himself .

But But that same week , Southwest received a $ 3.2 billion cash infusion from the Treasury to avoid having to apply for a loan . The infusion was the largest single airline aid package package provided through the CARES CARES Act , accounting for nearly nearly one - fourth of the total federal funding allocated to the airline airline industry . The funds were given to to carriers carriers to help them stay solvent and and keep their workers on the job . But one year after after receiving these these funds , customers of Southwest Airlines Airlines have have been been left wondering : Why has their service gotten worse instead of better ? Industrywide , the statistics are not encouraging . According According to to the the US Department of Transportation , there were more than 45,000 flight cancellations in November of 2020 . This is an increase of almost 20 percent from from the same period in 2019 . Customer complaints to the Department of Transportation have also jumped significantly , rising to 6,500 in October 2020 compared to around 2,500 in October of 2019 . The situation situation at Southwest Airlines has been even more more dire . Last summer summer , the airline had the highest rate of of canceled flights across the the entire US aviation industry . The airline has also faced criticism criticism for its handling of of customer service issues . text: Since the beginning beginning of the 20th century , American American corporations have been owned owned and operated by individuals , giving them the power to make decisions on behalf of their shareholders . But a new type of investor has has emerged in recent years that that is making waves in the corporate corporate world . These new investors are forcing companies to give back most most of their profits each each year and putting shareholder interests ahead of employees and customers . So - called private equity firms , hedge funds , and venture capital companies are buying buying stakes in public companies with with the intent of making a profit . These These firms are are forcing companies to share a substantial portion of their profits each each year , sometimes as as much as 90 percent percent . The The most notable private equity firm firm making waves in the the corporate world is the Blackstone Group . Blackstone is one of the largest private equity firms in the the world , with more than $ 567 billion in assets assets under management . The firm is well known for its aggressive tactics in acquiring companies and then extracting value from from them . Blackstone typically buys stakes in companies , but but instead of of taking control , it will will take a passive passive role role and pressure the company to to improve its performance performance . This typically typically involves cost - cutting , restructuring debt , and divesting unprofitable divisions . Once Blackstone is confident that the company is performing at at an acceptable level , it will will look to cash cash in its investment investment . Blackstone will then typically demand that the company pay out at least 90 percent of of its profits each year to its its investors . This This type type of investment has come under under increasing scrutiny in recent years , as it gives investors a quick return on on their investment investment and allows allows them to to walk away with with large large profits , while the company is left in a weakened state and unable to invest in new projects or reinvest in in its own operations . Critics have argued that this type of investment is is short - sighted and puts long - term economic growth and and job creation at risk . They argue that that these investments are hampering economic growth in the U.S. as companies are unable to invest invest in new projects or or hire hire new employees . In response to the the outcry , some companies have have started to to take a more shareholder - friendly approach . These companies are taking steps steps to ensure that their profits are reinvested back into the the business and and not solely given to investors . [[ ]] Companies like Apple and Microsoft Microsoft have have started to to focus on long - term returns for shareholders rather than short - term term gains . They are reinvesting profits in in research and development and providing competitive salaries salaries and benefits to to employees . By taking a long - term view and reinvesting in their own own operations , these companies are showing that there is is a way way for for companies to balance the interests of of investors and stakeholders . These companies companies are proving that that it is possible possible for companies to be both both profitable and sustainable for the long long - term . As the corporate landscape continues to to change , it is important for companies to be aware aware of the potential risks that come from giving too much of their profits to investors . Companies must find a balance balance that rewards shareholders while also providing value to to employees , customers , and the economy economy .
